verdict.rationale: Neon's own materials describe it as an open-source serverless Postgres platform that standard Postgres clients like psql and DBeaver connect to, and it documents the pgvector extension, so the core of real Postgres compatibility is supported. The evidence does not establish full parity with stock Postgres or a broad extension catalog, which is why this stays partial. Missing for 10: an explicit statement of upstream Postgres compatibility and supported versions, a documented list of supported extensions beyond pgvector, and independent hands-on corroboration that existing Postgres code runs unmodified.

support.subject: As a developer, I get real engine compatibility — the Postgres, MySQL, or SQLite dialect and extensions my existing code expects — not a lookalike subset

citations.quote: Neon is an open-source serverless Postgres database platform. It separates storage and compute
connect to it with your preferred Postgres client (psql, dbeaver, etc) or use the online SQL Editor
It enables us to build a much more cost-effective offering while keeping Postgres as our database.
